<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914519_theRebbe_363" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914519_theRebbe_363__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Shemini Atzeret is specifically the eighth day following Sukkot, where all the influences from the seven days of Sukkot are gathered and absorbed, creating a new festival in its own right.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">A)</t>
    <t s="2">And this is, "On the eighth day, it shall be a solemn assembly (Atzeret) for you,"</t>
    <t s="3">that it is called by the name "Shemini Atzeret" indicates that it comes specifically in continuation of the seven days of Sukkot,</t>
    <t s="4">even though on Shemini Atzeret the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are also gathered and absorbed,</t>
    <t s="5">for on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur it is the matter of ascent from below to above,</t>
    <t s="6">and since the intention is "to settle the world,"</t>
    <t s="7">an influence from above to below,</t>
    <t s="8">therefore it is called by the name "Shemini Atzeret,"</t>
    <t s="9">in which all the matters that were drawn down from above to below during the seven days of Sukkot are gathered and absorbed,</t>
    <t s="10">which is why it is specifically called "Shemini" (eighth)</t>
    <t s="11">[in addition to the fact that "Shemini" is related to the word "fat" and "oil"].</t>
    <t s="12">Nevertheless, Shemini Atzeret is a festival in its own right,</t>
    <t s="13">for through this very thing—that on Shemini Atzeret the matters of the seven days of Sukkot are gathered and absorbed—</t>
    <t s="14">a new matter is created in it,</t>
    <t s="15">a festival in its own right.</t>
    <t s="16">For during the seven days of Sukkot, there are drawn down</t>
    <t s="17">(in the manner of a surrounding light)</t>
    <t s="18">the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur and of the entire Ten Days of Repentance, until the completion of repentance on Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="19">and through the drawing down of this matter into inwardness and absorption on Shemini Atzeret,</t>
    <t s="20">"the day of our festival," in the singular,</t>
    <t s="21">there is revealed</t>
    <t s="22">(and in a manner of absorption)</t>
    <t s="23">the connection and unification of the aspect of Yechidah in the soul with the aspect of Yachid (the Singular One),</t>
    <t s="24">which is the goal of the matter of repentance,</t>
    <t s="25">"one bull, one ram."</t>
    <t s="26">And this is also "It shall be a solemn assembly (Atzeret) for you," and it is stated in the Midrash: "May they be yours alone, and no strangers with you,"</t>
    <t s="27">that this need to negate and say "no strangers with you" is because a baal teshuvah, whose nature is evil, requires extra caution,</t>
    <t s="28">and therefore one must negate the matter of "strangers"</t>
    <t s="29">(undesirable matters).</t>
    <t s="30">But through this very thing</t>
    <t s="31">(the extra caution of the baal teshuvah)</t>
    <t s="32">it becomes "May they be yours alone,"</t>
    <t s="33">for through the fact that repentance reaches His very Essence,</t>
    <t s="34">there is no place there for any giving of place to strangers,</t>
    <t s="35">"Israel and the King alone."</t>
    <t s="36">And on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="37">from the perspective of the drawing down of the Essence</t>
    <t s="38">(through the service of repentance)</t>
    <t s="39">the inner and true intention of the performance of undesirable matters is revealed,</t>
    <t s="40">that this was with prior intention</t>
    <t s="41">(as is known</t>
    <t s="42">regarding the matter of "terrible dealings with mankind")</t>
    <t s="43">in order that there be a transformation of darkness into light,</t>
    <t s="44">the turning of intentional sins into merits.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Simchat Torah is celebrated specifically on Shemini Atzeret for the sake of the second tablets, because the joy of the Torah elevates even the lowest aspects of the world and the soul, breaking through the limits of Torah itself to draw from the Essence.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">B)</t>
    <t s="2">And this is also why they established Simchat Torah on Shemini Atzeret specifically for the second tablets</t>
    <t s="3">[that the revelation of the second tablets</t>
    <t s="4">(the matter of repentance of Yom Kippur)</t>
    <t s="5">in inwardness and absorption is on Shemini Atzeret,</t>
    <t s="6">as above],</t>
    <t s="7">for the joy of Simchat Torah is</t>
    <t s="8">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="9">from the fact that the Torah also affects the lowest matters of the world,</t>
    <t s="10">and this is why the joy of Simchat Torah is with dancing with the feet, and specifically in the heels of them,</t>
    <t s="11">and therefore the joy is specifically for the second tablets,</t>
    <t s="12">the matter of repentance,</t>
    <t s="13">for through this, even the lowest of the world is refined,</t>
    <t s="14">until even intentional sins are turned into merits.</t>
    <t s="15">And just as in dancing</t>
    <t s="16">(physically),</t>
    <t s="17">through the feet and heels being lifted up</t>
    <t s="18">(they lift themselves)</t>
    <t s="19">and dancing,</t>
    <t s="20">they also lift up the head</t>
    <t s="21">(and the power of intellect within it)</t>
    <t s="22">so that it too dances with great joy beyond measure and limitation,</t>
    <t s="23">so too is it in the spiritual matters,</t>
    <t s="24">that through the joy and dancing of Simchat Torah, there is an ascent and elevation also in the aspect of the head of the soul.</t>
    <t s="25">And since "man is a microcosm,"</t>
    <t s="26">behold, through this there is an ascent and elevation, as it were, also in His wisdom, which is the Torah</t>
    <t s="27">[and this is also understood from the fact that in the dancing of the hakafot, the Torah itself also rejoices and dances,</t>
    <t s="28">as per the well-known statement of our Nesi'im],</t>
    <t s="29">and "joy breaks through boundaries,"</t>
    <t s="30">that the joy of Simchat Torah also breaks through the boundary of the Torah, as it were,</t>
    <t s="31">for the Torah in its own right is within measure and limitation, and through the joy and dancing of Simchat Torah, they draw into it from His Essence,</t>
    <t s="32">and as above, in the manner of the Sages' statement that Dovid would connect the upper Torah with the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="33">And just as it is with the Torah, so too is it with the souls of Israel,</t>
    <t s="34">that through the joy and dancing of Simchat Torah, there is an ascent and elevation in the aspect of the head of the soul</t>
    <t s="35">(as above),</t>
    <t s="36">that it becomes connected and literally one with the Essence,</t>
    <t s="37">"Lift up the head... to their skulls,"</t>
    <t s="38">that the main aspect of this will be in the tenth count, "the sheep shall again pass under the hand of the one who counts."</t>
    <t s="39">And all this is accomplished</t>
    <t s="40">(as above)</t>
    <t s="41">through our deeds and service during the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="42">and especially after the revelation of the Torah of Rashbi, and in the manner of "they will be sustained"</t>
    <t s="43">through the Torah of the Baal Shem Tov and through the Torah of Chabad Chassidus,</t>
    <t s="44">"and they will go out from exile with mercy,"</t>
    <t s="45">"and eternal joy upon their heads,"</t>
    <t s="46">in the true and complete redemption, very soon, with the coming of Moshiach Tzidkeinu,</t>
    <t s="47">Dovid Melech HaMoshiach.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
